The key to a good weekend is to stay up all day Friday and go to sleep at night, so we basically keep our buzz going all day to stay up.

Saturday morning, I wake up hungover, drive back to my place, and do whatever chores need to be done. It seems in quite a few anime / mangas, there are jokes about loli or characters who are straight up lolicons. I know here in the west, if any shows made jokes even somewhat similar they would be crucified and the show would probably be canceled. So, how exactly is lolicon thought of, and is it frowned upon as much as it is over here?
[Question] How is lolicon viewed in Japan?

Not an expert at all, but my sense of it is that like a lot of stuff in Japan it's fine as long as you're enjoying it in what's considered a socially appropriate way. So like, in places like Akihabara, Nakano and Ikebukuro which have a lot of shops around anime goods, you can find lolicon books, doujins and figures alongside other, non-loli goods in the same way you can find a lot of erotic material alongside non-H stuff. But like, given that being an otaku will already mean having a bad reputation in polite society, being considered a lolicon isn't going to be any better.

This is all just my opinion gathered and extrapolated from years of observation, reading articles and talking to Japanese loli artists. In Japan, lolicon is synonymous with pedophile for the most part, but since the stigma against pedophilia hasn't been anywhere near as big as in the West lolicons are/lolicon art is pretty much on the same level of stigma as white supremacists are here. It's not taboo to talk or joke about it in the right environment, but people still feel uneasy about the subject matter. In the last couple of years though, Japan has been forced to confront the subject matter of child porn(fake or not) through pressures from the West, namely UNICEF and some more influential G8 countries, so Japanese people are forced to either stand by that part of their culture or distance themselves from it, which a lot of uninvolved people naturally seem to prefer, because who wants to talk about things that make them uncomfortable, especially if it risk you loosing face, right? So yeah, there's still tolerance for it, especially from the hentai and art industry, but it's dwindling due to the political climate gradually acclimatizing people to a loli ban(they tried three of four times in the last 8 years), and the country being put on the spot for it by the West in the media, especially with the Olympics coming up and a lot of Western tourists posing a danger of causing an international faux pas.

Imagine Japan's stance to regarding lolicon comparable to what Western loli would have been perceived as in the West during the late 70s and early 80s. People wouldn't have been completely conditioned that pedophilia and anything related to it is equal to or leading up to child rape, that there is no difference between child abuse, child adult sex and pedophilia, and so on. If you want to see where Japans future lies regarding their stance towards lolicon, just look at Western countries today. Yep, not a particularly bright future it is.
